dataset.definition: A collected batch of measured numbers, such as wind speeds, ocean temperatures, or ice thickness readings, organized in rows and columns for scientists to analyze.

metadata.definition: Simple summary details that tell you who collected a file, what day it was recorded, where the expedition went, and what instruments were used.

coordinates.definition: Two numbers (latitude and longitude) that pinpoint an exact spot on Earth's surface, measured in degrees north/south of the equator and east/west of the prime meridian.

latitude.definition: Distance north or south of Earth's equator. The North Pole is at 90 degrees North, and the South Pole is at 90 degrees South.

longitude.definition: Distance east or west of the prime meridian line in Greenwich, helping pinpoint positions across the globe.

projection.definition: A mathematical method used to draw Earth's curved, spherical surface onto a flat screen or paper map.

publication.definition: A formal scientific paper or research report reviewed and published in an academic journal so other researchers worldwide can review the discoveries.

doi.definition: A permanent unique web link assigned to a scientific publication that does not change.

activity.definition: Public outreach events, school video calls, live science exhibits, and station celebrations conducted by expedition members to connect with citizens.

report.definition: A written record prepared by the voyage team summarizing daily logs, observations, and science operations.

status.definition: Indicates whether an expedition is currently active in the field, completed and back home, or planned for an upcoming season.

completed.definition: The expedition crew has concluded field research, safely returned home, and archived their samples and initial reports.

active.definition: The expedition crew or automated sensors are currently on site at the research station or ship, actively logging new observations.

planned.definition: An upcoming voyage scheduled for future seasonal deployment, currently finalizing logistics, crew training, and equipment staging.

region.definition: The major cold polar geographical zone where the mission operates: Antarctica (South Pole), Arctic (North Pole), or the Southern Ocean.

expedition.definition: A planned journey of scientists, engineers, and logistical specialists dispatched to high-latitude environments to conduct research for months or years.

year.definition: The calendar year during which the expedition departed from port or began primary field measurements.

tags.definition: Simple topic keywords (like #ice, #wildlife, #ocean) assigned to help visitors quickly find matching records.
